item.title: Fourier-Guided Multi-Scale Vision Transformer for Object-Independent Detection and Severity Grading of Rain-Induced Cracking in Sweet Cherry
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hoa-Cuc. Nguyen, Ngoc-Duong. Nguyen, Viet-Hung. Pham, Bich-Ngoc. Mach, Trinh Thi Nhu Quynh, Thanh Q. Nguyen
Rain-induced cracking is among the most damaging preharvest disorders of sweet cherry because even narrow cuticular fractures reduce fresh-market value and create entry sites for water loss and fungal infection. Conventional inspection is subjective and is least reliable for low-contrast microcracks near the pedicel cavity. This study developed a Fourier-guided multi-scale Vision Transformer (FGM-ViT) for joint fruit-level severity grading and pixel-level crack segmentation. The dataset comprised 960 individual fruit from four commercial cultivars and eight orchard blocks, imaged from four rotational views after natural rainfall exposure or controlled water-immersion challenge. item.title: Dominant Role of Solid Matrix and Persistent Free Radicals in Cr(VI) Reduction by Biochar
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Zhe Ding, Jianjun Liang, Longmiao Yuan, Wentao Zhang, Beihang Zhang, Huiyang Mei 等8位作者
Biochar has emerged as a promising material for remediating toxic hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)), yet the distinct roles of its soluble components and solid matrix remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated the mechanisms of Cr(VI) immobilization by rice husk biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures (200–600°C). The biochar pyrolyzed at 400°C (RH400) exhibits the highest Cr(VI) reduction efficiency, effectively converting Cr(VI) to less toxic Cr(III). Through comparative experiments with biochar leachate and the residual solid matrix, we demonstrate that the soluble leachate does not contribute to Cr(VI) reduction, but instead antagonizes total chromium immobilization by competing for sorption sites. item.title: Initial Conformation Governs Amyloid-β42 Dynamics and Association at a POPC Membrane-Water Interface
item.description:

👤 Yersultan Arynbek, Khlood A.A.A. Abdeljawaad, Duc Huy Le, Kahramon Mamatkulov, Grigory Arzumanyan
The conformational heterogeneity of amyloid-β42 (Aβ42) may influence its early interactions with lipid membranes, yet the extent to which different initial structures determine subsequent membrane association remains unclear. Here, three nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) derived Aβ42 monomer structures (1IYT, 1Z0Q, and 6SZF) were examined at a 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-phosphocholine (POPC) membrane-water interface. Despite an identical environment, the monomers followed different trajectories during comparative 200-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the CHARMM36m force field. The predominantly α-helical 1IYT structure underwent substantial relaxation, with α-helical content decreasing from 78.57% to 44.77%. Carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastic (CFRTP) composites present a recyclable alternative to traditional thermosets, yet fully realizing their structural potential remains constrained by the chemical incompatibility between commercial epoxy-based sizing on the surface of carbon fibers and high-viscosity thermoplastic matrices such as polycarbonate (PC). item.title: Experimental Correlation of Electrical and Optical Noise in a DFB Laser: Implications for Quantum Key Distribution and Quantum Random Number Generation
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Imad ASAAD
We present an experimental and analytical study of the electrical-optical noise correlation in a distributed-feedback (DFB) laser diode operating at 1550 nm. Using dual-channel fast Fourier transform (FFT) measurements, we extract the power spectral densities of the injection current noise, the relative intensity noise (RIN) and their cross-spectrum. From these, the spectral coherence CI−P (f ) is computed, revealing a strong correlation at low frequencies ( 0.82). We quantify the impact of this correlation on two quantum communication technologies. For quantum key distribution (QKD), we evaluate the information leakage and show that with standard low-noise electronics it remains negligible. item.title: Cold-Alkaline Processed Enset (Ensete Ventricosum) Starch: Optimization of Gel Formation, Neutralization, and Formulation for Cosmetic and Adhesive Applications
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Mitiku Muanenda, Olika Mamo, Yobsan Lemi
Background Enset (Ensete ventricosum) is a staple food crop in Ethiopia, traditionally processed into kocho and bulla (purified starch). While enset starch possesses favorable physicochemical properties including high purity (99.24%), 29% amylose content, and B-type crystallinity, its industrial applications remain largely unexplored. item.title: Disproportionate Contributions of Baseflow to Nitrogen and Phosphorus Export in an Agricultural Watershed of Southwest China
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Mingmin Li, Qiuying Shen, Hailong Wang, Haitao Feng, Leilin Yang, Guoqing Li 等10位作者
Baseflow is a stable runoff component fed by groundwater, yet its contribution to nutrient export from agricultural watersheds in the Erhai Lake region remains poorly quantified. We addressed this gap by analyzing daily discharge and monthly water quality data from 2015 to 2024 in the Miju River catchment, using Eckhardt digital filtering, LOADEST load estimation, and XGBoost attribution to separate baseflow, estimate nitrogen and phosphorus fluxes, and rank their driving factors. Baseflow accounted for only 40.9% of total runoff but delivered 44.3% of total nitrogen and 55.9% of total phosphorus, revealing a disproportionate role especially for phosphorus. item.title: Rethinking Surface-Layer Parameterization: A Turbulence-Based Framework Without Using Similarity Functions and Its Impacts on Surface–Atmosphere Coupling
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Kiran Alapaty, Jimy Dudhia, Pedro A Jiminéz, Wei Wang, Temple R Lee
This study introduces and evaluates a new surface-layer formulation implemented in the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model in which turbulent exchange is represented using a 3D turbulence velocity scale, (:e*), thereby avoiding the explicit use of Monin–Obukhov similarity functions that have formed the basis of atmospheric surface-layer parameterizations for more than five decades. In this framework, stability dependence is embedded within the turbulence velocity scale itself, allowing surface–atmosphere exchange to emerge dynamically from the evolving turbulent and thermodynamic state of the boundary-layer. item.title: When accuracy does not improve decisions: a decision-outcome validation framework for cross-regional box office forecasting
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Lu Chao, Xu AnQi, XiaoXi Ma
Cross-regional box office forecasting is routinely evaluated with predictive accuracy on randomly split samples, yet the models that minimize root mean squared error are not necessarily the models that produce better market selection decisions. This paper develops a decision-outcome validation framework in which forecast models are compared through a budget-constrained market selection problem, using temporal walk-forward holdouts, region-out and film-out generalization protocols, and top-k payoff, regret and hit rate as the evaluation criteria. The framework is applied to a web-sourced panel of 14 Chinese films released between 2023 and 2025, covering 76 film market pairs and 18 overseas territories with weekly gross data.
